text:
Pepperdine University to host Human-Centered AI Conference and Global Summit on Faith in AI
M. S. Mccall
Pepperdine University will host the sixth annual Human-Centered AI Conference and the inaugural Global Summit on Faith in AI this fall, according to a Sep. 16 announcement. The events are scheduled for September 25-26 at the university's Malibu campus.
The two-day event will bring together leading artificial intelligence practitioners, researchers, corporate executives, and global religious figures to discuss how artificial intelligence could positively affect the human condition. Attendees will have opportunities to gain new insights into AI development while considering its moral and ethical implications.
Fabien Scalzo, associate professor of computer science at Seaver College, director of Pepperdine’s Keck Data Science Institute, and chair of the conference, said, “Pepperdine’s Human-Centered AI Conference is an exciting opportunity to hear how some of the world’s leading AI experts are trying to harness these new tools to better humanity.” Scalzo added that this year’s event aims to broaden the conversation by exploring how faith should influence technology use in line with Pepperdine's Christian mission.
The conference will feature academics such as Judea Pearl from UCLA, Paul Thompson from USC, and Katie Bouman from Caltech alongside CEOs like Leo Petrossian (Kandu Inc.), Matthew Johnson, and Josh Bloom (Valency). The Global Summit on Faith in AI will include faith leaders such as Rabbi Erez Sherman (Sinai Temple), Archbishop Thomas Paul Schirrmacher, His Eminence Metropolitan Gerasimos of San Francisco representing Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew. Johnnie Moore—Pepperdine vice chancellor and managing director of Middle East studies—will chair this summit. Moore said, “You don’t have to be a religious Christian like me to appreciate religion as a kind of wisdom compounding across the centuries... Artificial intelligence forces those questions on all of us at once, and we’d be foolish to take them up without the people who’ve been thinking about them the whole time.”
Recent Pepperdine alumni working in artificial intelligence—including Sean Wu (the university's first Rhodes Scholar), Ulysse Saltiel, Katelin Goño, and Yuning Yang—will also participate by sharing their professional experiences. Scalzo said, “We’re so excited to welcome our talented alumni back to campus. They are the ones who will help shape the future of AI. Their wisdom, insight, and accomplishments all exemplify the impact Pepperdine students can go on to make in their vocational fields.”
The conference program includes keynote lectures, panel discussions with industry experts and faith leaders, sessions led by alumni professionals in artificial intelligence fields, as well as networking opportunities for attendees.
